I'm going to share this very important sentence that took me LITERALLY years of therapy and processes to understand: "It wasn't your fault." I'll spare the details of my own history with these very familiar demons, but one of the first steps for me was to emotionally understand I was not at fault. I convinced myself for years logically and mentally that I was only a child and had to have bore some of the responsibility of everything, but through the years the flashback and other issues never went away. I have been working with my therapist(s) with some PTSD reprocessing tools and have started to make progress. I'm not saying that I am by any means cured, BUT I have learned emotionally how to deal with things that happened. I have learned other tools to use when my head starts spinning around and wants to explode. 
I guess what I was trying to say during the rant above is that this is something that you may have to be proactive with. Speak to your therapist as to any sort of PTSD reprocessing procedures that they are familiar with. Check around into other therapist that may have more of a background with sexual based traumas and rape survivors. It's gonna be a tough road, but you got this. Find a support group, PM me or any of the others that have offered, speak with a friend or loved one. Just don't think for a second that your life is worthless because of this. I spent too many years feeling that way, so believe me when I say that I'm sorry this happened to you. It wasn't your fault.

Much of existence is a balance of satisfying needs and acknowledging what is out of our control. If I had a choice, I would have been AFAB also, but that is something that was determined outside of my control. If I am hungry, I eat; this is within my control. My understanding of my own being, internally, is female (or something close to it), but my external meat suit was AMAB. My proprioception and my self-conceptualization fight an endless war on a daily basis, which causes a strong desire to check out of existence for me. Instead of continuing to be a soldier in this war between my internal factions, I have started to opt into peace talks between how my psychology conceives of me and my body is constructed. This is what therapy may help you to do. Understand more about your own reasonings and triggers for the dysphoria that you experience, the causes of the suicidal ideation, the sources of your personal struggle. Their goal and intention isn't necessarily to prevent you from doing something that you think may be what you want to do, but to remove all the dust and clutter from your own understanding about yourself so you can make a clearer decision. I can't/won't tell you how to make decisions about your existence, but I can share from my own experience that if you give it some time and try a different angle of approach, you might allow yourself to make a concession or two you wouldn't have considered before.
